title: Same band plays dances; white society engagements and rehearsals
summary: The same fourteen men played the evening dance, including white dances at the Battle House and clubs; they read music and rehearsed twice weekly.

story.theme_name: Playing for dancers: dance bands and the dances themselves
story.community_name: Dancing to the band: quadrilles, waltzes and dance sets

blocks.x: Right. And on that night, we'd return around eight o'clock to the place where they would have the dance. Yes. Then we'd put into music to the dance with the same band.
Same band, yes. Same band, same band.
Same band. You had fourteen men in the dance band? Fourteen men in the dance band.
We had... We played all the popular airs, you know, just as they come up.

And the same... That was colored. We made those plays, you know. Yes. Now we played all the white dances downtown, which we had the famous band in town. We played the Battle House, Country Club, and the Athelston Club, all that was big...
Did you always play written music or did you play written music? Or did you sometimes play... No, no, no, no.
Sometimes we'd pick up or something, you know. They were very good at that. Yes.
Coming back from the cemetery, I guess you played by head or by ear? I don't mean by ear or by music. Yes. We had music, sure.
We were rehearsing on an average twice a week. And if a member of the band wasn't there at that time, why, he was fine. So, you know, back in those days, 25 cents, for instance.
